signals.name: SENSITIVE_CONFIG_KEY
signals.description: A configuration key whose own name matches the sensitive-key pattern (password|pwd|secret|token|apikey|api_key|connectionstring|accountkey|sharedaccesskey|credential) and whose last word does not merely describe a secret (Type, Name, Path, Dir, Url, Endpoint, Provider, Header ... : ClientCredentialType, TokenEndpoint and SecretsDir are settings) — presence only, value never read (Part G). Also read from Web Deploy SetParameters files (SetParam*.xml, SetParameters*.xml by the engagement's globs) of the project.
signals.value_semantics: one row per distinct matching key; value is the key's full configuration path (Section:Sub:Key for JSON, the appSettings key or attribute name for XML, the parameter name for SetParameters), never the secret

signals.name: ENCODING_DEFAULT_USAGE
signals.description: Access to System.Text.Encoding.Default: the ANSI code page on .NET Framework, always UTF-8 on .NET Core and later.
signals.value_semantics: the fully qualified member, System.Text.Encoding.Default; one row per file, a line span per use. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: DATETIME_NOW_USAGE
signals.description: Access to DateTime.Now, DateTime.Today or DateTimeOffset.Now: host-local time, which is UTC in a default Linux container.
signals.value_semantics: the fully qualified member (System.DateTime.Now, System.DateTime.Today, System.DateTimeOffset.Now); one row per distinct member per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: USE_WINDOWS_SERVICE_INVOCATION
signals.description: A UseWindowsService() or AddWindowsService() call: the generic host runs as a Windows Service.
signals.value_semantics: the method called (UseWindowsService or AddWindowsService); one row per distinct method per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: SYSTEM_DRAWING_USAGE
signals.description: A Windows-only System.Drawing (GDI+) type used in code: Bitmap, Graphics, Image, Font, Brush, Pen, Icon and similar. Cross-platform System.Drawing.Primitives types (Color, Point, Size, Rectangle) are not matched.
signals.value_semantics: the fully qualified type; one row per distinct type per file. Matched when written fully qualified, or when the file imports System.Drawing. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: REGISTRY_ACCESS_USAGE
signals.description: Access to the Windows registry through Microsoft.Win32.Registry or RegistryKey.OpenBaseKey/OpenRemoteBaseKey.
signals.value_semantics: the fully qualified member, e.g. Microsoft.Win32.Registry.LocalMachine; one row per distinct member per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: DIRECTORY_SERVICES_USAGE
signals.description: Use of System.DirectoryServices or System.DirectoryServices.AccountManagement types (DirectoryEntry, DirectorySearcher, PrincipalContext, *Principal), which are Windows-only. System.DirectoryServices.Protocols works on Linux and is not matched.
signals.value_semantics: the fully qualified type; one row per distinct type per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: PROCESS_START_USAGE
signals.description: A Process.Start call or new ProcessStartInfo: launching an executable or shell, whose name and arguments usually assume Windows. Presence only; the command and arguments are never recorded.
signals.value_semantics: System.Diagnostics.Process.Start or System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo; one row per distinct member per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: ADD_HEALTH_CHECKS_INVOCATION
signals.description: An AddHealthChecks() call registering ASP.NET Core health check services.
signals.value_semantics: the method called, AddHealthChecks; one row per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: MAP_HEALTH_CHECKS_INVOCATION
signals.description: A MapHealthChecks() or UseHealthChecks() call exposing a health endpoint an OCP4 probe can target.
signals.value_semantics: the method called (MapHealthChecks or UseHealthChecks); one row per distinct method per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method or type name.

signals.name: WINDOWS_PATH_LITERAL
signals.description: A Windows drive-letter path (C:\..., G:/...) in a C# string literal or a configuration value. Comments are never read; neither is any connection string or sensitive-key value (Part G). Also read from Web Deploy SetParameters files (SetParam*.xml, SetParameters*.xml by the engagement's globs) of the project, by the same rules.
signals.value_semantics: the matched path; one row per distinct path per file, each evidence entry carrying matchedValue. sourceType tells source code from configuration.

signals.name: UNC_PATH_LITERAL
signals.description: A UNC share path (\\server\share\...) in a C# string literal or a configuration value. Device paths (\\?\, \\.\) are not matched. Same Part G exclusions as WINDOWS_PATH_LITERAL. Also read from Web Deploy SetParameters files (SetParam*.xml, SetParameters*.xml by the engagement's globs) of the project, by the same rules.
signals.value_semantics: the matched path; one row per distinct path per file, each evidence entry carrying matchedValue. sourceType tells source code from configuration.

signals.name: UNQUALIFIED_HOSTNAME_URL
signals.description: A URL (http, https, net.tcp, net.pipe, ws, wss, ftp) whose host is a single label such as appsrv0341, in a C# string literal, a configuration value or a SetParameters value. It resolves on Windows through NetBIOS or the DNS suffix search; in an OpenShift pod only if the cluster's DNS search domains cover it. localhost, IP addresses and placeholders are not matched; secret-named values and connection strings are never read.
signals.value_semantics: the host only, lowercased — never the URL's path, query or credentials; one row per distinct host per file.

signals.name: SERILOG_FILE_SINK_CONFIG
signals.description: A Serilog sink named File or RollingFile under the Serilog section of appsettings*.json, including one nested in an Async sink's configure.
signals.value_semantics: the sink's Args.path value (null when absent); one row per distinct path per file.

signals.name: WINDOWS_AUTH_CONNECTION_STRING_CONFIG
signals.description: A connection string that authenticates with the process's Windows identity (Integrated Security / SSPI / Trusted_Connection), which does not exist in a Linux container. The two keywords are synonyms and the last one written wins, as in SqlClient. The string is parsed in memory for those keywords and discarded (Part G). Also read from Web Deploy SetParameters files (SetParam*.xml, SetParameters*.xml by the engagement's globs) of the project, by the same rules.
signals.value_semantics: the connection string's name only; nothing derived from the string itself is ever recorded.

signals.name: WCF_CLIENT_ENDPOINT_CONFIG
signals.description: An <endpoint> element under system.serviceModel/client: this code calls a WCF service.
signals.value_semantics: the endpoint's contract; the binding type is WCF_BINDING_CONFIG.

signals.name: KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG
signals.description: A Kafka bootstrap servers setting (BootstrapServers, bootstrap.servers) in configuration.
signals.value_semantics: the key path, e.g. Kafka:BootstrapServers, never the hosts. Name-based: confidence 0.8.

signals.name: REDIS_CONNECTION_CONFIG
signals.description: A Redis connection setting: a connection string or configuration section whose name contains 'redis'.
signals.value_semantics: the key path of the topmost matching key, never the value (it usually carries a password). Name-based: confidence 0.8.

signals.name: VAULT_CONFIG
signals.description: A HashiCorp Vault settings section: a configuration key whose name contains 'vault' but not 'keyvault' (Azure Key Vault is a different product and is not matched).
signals.value_semantics: the key path of the topmost matching key, never a value; tokens inside it are SENSITIVE_CONFIG_KEY. Name-based: confidence 0.8.

signals.value_semantics: the package id.

signals.name: MICROSOFT_EXTENSIONS_HOSTING_WINDOWSSERVICES_PACKAGE

signals.name: WCF_CLIENT_PACKAGE
signals.description: A .NET WCF client package (System.ServiceModel.Http, .NetTcp, .Primitives, .Duplex, .Security, .Federation), read from step 2's inventory. Client-side only; server-side WCF on .NET is CoreWCF.

signals.value_semantics: count of matching files

signals.name: WCF_CLIENT_BINDING_CONFIG
signals.description: The binding type of an <endpoint> under system.serviceModel/client: the binding this code calls a WCF service with. Unlike WCF_BINDING_CONFIG, which records every endpoint's binding without saying whose, this is client endpoints only.
signals.value_semantics: the binding type, e.g. netTcpBinding; one row per distinct binding per file.

signals.name: WCF_CLIENT_BINDING_USAGE
signals.description: A WCF binding constructed in client code (new NetTcpBinding(), new BasicHttpBinding() ...), as dotnet-svcutil generates: only in a file that derives ClientBase<T> or creates a ChannelFactory<T>, and never in one that mentions ServiceHost or AddServiceEndpoint. The code-configured counterpart of WCF_CLIENT_BINDING_CONFIG.
signals.value_semantics: the fully qualified binding type, e.g. System.ServiceModel.NetTcpBinding; one row per distinct binding per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.8.

signals.name: PACKAGE_UPGRADE_SAFE
signals.description: A direct package with a newer version that supports the engagement's target framework, and an upgrade that changes nothing the code calls: by API diff; because the package is a build, tools, analyzer or content package with no compile-time assemblies; or, where no diff is possible, a minor or patch change (semver heuristic).
signals.value_semantics: '{id} {from} -> {to}'. One row per project per package, located at the PackageReference (or packages.config) line. Confidence 0.85 from the API diff, 0.8 by package kind, 0.5 from the semver heuristic. A content package moving a major version is still this signal; the artifact flags it contentBreakingPossible (markup or CSS may break).

signals.name: PACKAGE_UPGRADE_BREAKING
signals.description: A direct runtime package (one with lib/ or ref/ assemblies) whose recommended version removes or changes a public member the code calls. Must be fixed in the same unit of work as the version bump (package-upgrade-safe and package-upgrade-breaking run together).
signals.value_semantics: '{id} {from} -> {to}: {member}'. One row per affected file and changed member, a line span per call site; syntax-only call-site matching. Confidence 0.7 when a call site in the file is confirmed, 0.4 when every call site there is ambiguous (an unchanged overload accepts the same arguments). Where no API diff was possible and semver presumes a break, one row at the PackageReference line with ': (major version; call sites not determined)', confidence 0.5.

signals.name: PACKAGE_NO_COMPATIBLE_VERSION
signals.description: A direct package with no version on the authoritative feed that supports the engagement's target framework: a replacement, not an upgrade.
signals.value_semantics: '{id} {current}'. One row per project per package, located at the PackageReference (or packages.config) line. Confidence 0.9.

signals.name: PACKAGE_DEPRECATED
signals.description: A direct package whose current version the feed marks deprecated. A flag: co-occurs with any upgrade outcome, and upgrading does not clear it.
signals.value_semantics: '{id} {current}: {replacement}' — the publisher's suggested replacement package, or 'no suggested replacement'. One row per project per package, located at the PackageReference (or packages.config) line. Confidence 0.85.

signals.name: PACKAGE_VULNERABLE
signals.description: A direct package whose current version has a published vulnerability advisory. A flag: co-occurs with any upgrade outcome.
signals.value_semantics: '{id} {current}: {severity}' — the highest severity, low | moderate | high | critical. One row per project per package, located at the PackageReference (or packages.config) line. Confidence 0.85.

signals.name: PACKAGE_NOT_IN_CLIENT_FEED
signals.description: A direct package whose newest compatible version on nuget.org is newer than anything the client feed holds: the upgrade needs the version approved into the client's feed first. Only when client feeds are declared.
signals.value_semantics: '{id}: latest public compatible {latestPublicVersion}, latest in {feedName} {latestInClientFeed or none}'. One row per project per package, located at the PackageReference (or packages.config) line. Confidence 0.85.

signals.name: EXPOSES_WCF_SERVICE
signals.description: The project implements a WCF service contract — wherever the contract is declared and however the service is hosted. Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: the service contract; one row per contract per implementing file, evidence the implementing class and its operations.

signals.name: WCF_SERVICE_HOSTING
signals.description: Where a service this project implements is hosted: a ServiceHost, an IIS .svc file or CoreWCF, in which project or folder (a folder of .svc files with no project file is named as such). On the implementing project. Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: '<ServiceHost|IIS .svc|CoreWCF> in <project or folder>', or 'no host found'; one row per host per file.

signals.name: HOSTS_WCF_SERVICE
signals.description: The project constructs a ServiceHost (or CoreWCF host) for, or holds the .svc file of, a WCF service — the process the service runs in, not the code that implements it. Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: the hosted service contract; one row per contract per hosting file, evidence the host construction or .svc file.

signals.name: EXPOSES_HTTP_API
signals.description: The project exposes HTTP endpoints: MVC or Web API controller actions, or minimal APIs. Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: the controller or handler type; one row per type per file.

signals.name: EXPOSES_ASMX_SERVICE
signals.description: The project exposes an ASMX web service ([WebMethod] on a WebService). Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: the service path (/Catalog/PicUploader.asmx); one row per service per file.

signals.name: EXPOSES_GRPC_SERVICE
signals.description: The project implements a gRPC service (a generated Service.ServiceBase subclass). Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: the gRPC service name; one row per service per file.

signals.name: EXPOSES_WEBFORMS_UI
signals.description: The project serves Web Forms pages (.aspx with a code-behind Page class). Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from its resolved entry points, application origin only.
signals.value_semantics: the page path (/About.aspx); one row per page.

signals.name: INTERACTIVE_CONSOLE_INPUT
signals.description: The program needs a person at the keyboard: Console.ReadKey (which throws when there is no console or input is redirected), a Console.Read or ReadLine whose result is used, or an interactive prompt library (Spectre.Console prompts, Sharprompt). A scheduled or containerised job has no one to answer it.
signals.value_semantics: the member ('System.Console.ReadKey', 'System.Console.ReadLine', 'Spectre.Console.TextPrompt', 'Sharprompt.Prompt.Select'); one row per member per file, a line span per use.

signals.name: CONSOLE_PAUSE_FOR_INPUT
signals.description: A Console.Read or ReadLine whose result is discarded: 'Press ENTER to exit', or a self-hosted service waiting to be stopped. With no console it returns at once rather than blocking, so it does not prove a person is needed — but a host that waits on it to stay alive exits immediately in a container.
signals.value_semantics: the member ('System.Console.ReadLine'); one row per member per file, a line span per use.

signals.name: AMBIGUOUS_TOP_LEVEL_PROGRAM_ON_NET10
signals.description: From .NET 10, ASP.NET Core generates a public Program for a web project whose entry point is top-level statements. A project that references two or more projects whose Program is then public, and names Program (WebApplicationFactory<Program>), no longer compiles: CS0433. On earlier frameworks the implicit Program is internal, so only an explicit public partial class Program was visible. Emitted by lifecycle step 4 (entry-point-inventory) from step 2's project references and SDKs and each project's top-level statements.
signals.value_semantics: the file holding the top-level statements of a referenced project whose Program becomes public only on net10.0 (where the fix goes); located at the consuming file that names Program, a line per use. One row per such referenced project.

signals.name: TARGET_FRAMEWORK_BELOW_ENGAGEMENT_TARGET
signals.description: A .NET Core or .NET 5+ project (.NETCoreApp) whose target framework is below the engagement's target framework (engagements.target_framework). Emitted by lifecycle step 6 (dependency-assessment), which is given the engagement's target.
signals.value_semantics: '{from} -> {to}', located at the line declaring the target framework: the project file, else the nearest Directory.Build.props above it that declares one.

signals.name: PACKAGE_PROVIDED_BY_FRAMEWORK
signals.description: A direct package the target framework's shared framework already provides, at a version it carries (the SDK's PackageOverrides.txt, schemas/shared-frameworks-1.0.0.json): Microsoft.NETCore.App's for every project, Microsoft.AspNetCore.App's for a Web or Razor SDK project or one with a FrameworkReference to it. A removal, not an upgrade: dependency-assessment outcome framework_provided.
signals.value_semantics: '{id} {from}: provided by {shared framework} {target}'. One row per project per package, located at the PackageReference line.

signals.name: USE_IIS_INVOCATION
signals.description: A UseIIS() or UseIISIntegration() call: the application is hosted behind IIS through the ASP.NET Core Module.
signals.value_semantics: the method called (UseIIS or UseIISIntegration); one row per distinct method per file. Syntax-only: confidence 0.9 for a type-qualified member, 0.8 for a bare method name.

signals.name: ASPNETCORE_HOSTING_MODEL
signals.description: How an ASP.NET Core application is hosted in IIS through the ASP.NET Core Module: the project file's <AspNetCoreHostingModel>, a web.config's <aspNetCore hostingModel>, or the module handler (modules="AspNetCoreModule[V2]") with no model stated.
signals.value_semantics: inprocess, outofprocess or unspecified; located at the declaring line.

signals.name: CONTAINER_RUNS_AS_ROOT
signals.description: An existing Dockerfile whose final stage never switches to a non-root user or switches to root, or a manifest setting runAsUser: 0, runAsNonRoot: false, privileged: true or allowPrivilegeEscalation: true. OpenShift's restricted security context constraint refuses it.
signals.value_semantics: the instruction or manifest line as written ('no USER instruction: the image runs as root' when absent), located at its line. Repository-level for a file outside every project directory.

signals.name: CONTAINER_PRIVILEGED_PORT
signals.description: An existing Dockerfile or manifest binding a port below 1024: EXPOSE, a listening URL or port variable (ASPNETCORE_URLS, ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS, HTTP_PORTS) in the final stage, or a containerPort. A non-root process cannot bind it.
signals.value_semantics: the instruction or manifest line as written, located at its line.

signals.name: CONTAINER_FIXED_USER_WRITABLE_PATH
signals.description: Writable paths that assume a fixed user: a chown in the final stage to an owner whose group is not 0, or an owner-only chmod (700, 600), with no later chmod giving group 0 the owner's rights (g=u); or a manifest's fixed runAsUser or fsGroup. OpenShift runs the image with an arbitrary UID in group 0.
signals.value_semantics: the instruction or manifest line as written, located at its line.
